title: Shut Down Moshannon Protest

location.venue: Philipsburg Memorial Park, across the street from the Philipsburg Borough Office located at

description:
Indivisible groups across Pennsylvania are on a mission to SHUT DOWN MOSHANNON!

Moshannon Valley Processing Center, located in Clearfield County, is the largest Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facility in the Northeastern United States. Operated by the for-profit prison corporation GEO Group, this facility has become a central hub for detaining immigrants—many of whom have no criminal record and are being held without due process.

People from across the region—Pennsylvania, Ohio, New Jersey, and beyond—are being transported to this remote prison, hidden from public view but not from public outrage. Inside its walls, detainees face isolation, substandard medical care, and a long record of human rights violations documented by legal advocates and watchdog organizations.
The facility operates under a contract between ICE and the Clearfield County Commissioners—a contract that is set to expire in 2026. That gives us a critical window to act. We must send a powerful message: 

Pennsylvania will not be complicit in the cruelty of immigration detention.

We say NO to indefinite detention without trial.
We say NO to families being torn apart.
We say NO to profiting off of human suffering.

It’s time to demand that Clearfield County officials end their contract with ICE—and that GEO Group gets out of our state for good.

Join the movement. Stand up. Speak out.
SHUT DOWN MOSHANNON.

title: Protect Our Checks! Rally in Wilkes-Barre for Social Security
description:
On Saturday, August 16th, we are gathering right here in Wilkes-Barre and all across the country to urge our members of Congress to safeguard one of their most vital sources of income for families: Social Security.

Join Affordable Pennsylvania, Action Together NEPA, Pennsylvanians Together, and Pennsylvania Policy Center as we stand up for Social Security and demand Congress protect what we’ve earned.

**In honor of the 90th Anniversary of the Social Security Act, let's PROTECT OUR CHECKS!** 

------------------------------------

**EVENT INFO**

**Parking and Transportation:**

For those coming to the Protect Our Checks Rally in downtown Wilkes-Barre, there are multiple locations within walking distance where you can park! Wilkes-Barre has metered parking available around Public Square and throughout Downtown Wilkes-Barre. Meter parking is $1.00 an hour, and you can use quarters, dimes, and nickels at the meters. There is also an app that you can use to pay, called PANGO. Additionally, Wilkes-Barre has several parking garages nearby. Please note that the Intermodal Parking Garage is accessible, with an elevator. We look forward to seeing you!

Public Square is wheelchair accessible at all corners. If you need any additional assistance, please find an Action Together staff member and they will assist you.

**What to Wear:** 

This will be a rain or shine event, so be sure to dress in weather appropriate clothing and footwear allowing you to stay comfortable for up to two hours. Wear sunscreen!

**Bring Signs!**

Homemade signs are always the best. Get creative! Here are some suggestions if you need them: 

- Protect Our Checks 
- Hands Off Social Security
- Social Security Works - Billionaires Don’t!
- Its OUR Social Security
- Protect Our Checks (And Balances!)
- People Over Profits

title: Grandview Rush Hour Rally
description:
Join us in standing up for our future and protesting the Trump administration’s reckless economic policies that put profit over people. His massive tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy will explode the national deficit, opening the door to devastating cuts to Medicaid, SNAP, Social Security, education, research and more—the very lifelines and services millions of families depend on. Tariffs and trade wars will spike prices on groceries, clothing, and everyday goods, squeezing working families while small businesses fight to stay afloat. His harsh immigration policies are also draining our workforce, hurting industries like agriculture, construction, and hospitality that keep our economy moving. These aren’t distant policy choices—they mean higher bills, fewer resources, job losses and harder decisions for ordinary Americans. Raise your voice and demand an economy that works for everyone, not just the rich and powerful.

Organized by Grandview Ignite. 

Signage recommendations: During our weekly rallies our goal is to reach out to as many people as possible (D’s, R’s & undecided voters) as they drive by. Keep your sentences short so that car occupants can read them as they drive by. Please, focus your messages on the negative economic impacts of the Big Beautiful Bill, the negative impacts of the Immigration policies, and the negative impacts of the import Tariffs will all have on the lives of everyday Americans rather than attacking Trump himself. We do not want to lower ourselves to his gutter level. Truth to power is what we are after. Here are a few examples:
•       Medicaid cuts = insurance & medicine costs skyrocket.
•       ICE raids = Who is going to pick our crops?
•       Tariffs = Tax on all of us!

Safety tips for attending rallies in hot weather:
wear a wide brimmed hat and light colored, breathable clothing
drink plenty of water
at the first sign of heat illness (dizziness, muscle cramps, headache, nausea) move to a cooler location and slowly drink a cool beverage. Seek medical attention if you do not feel better. (WA State Dept of Health)
Your safety is our top concern. If you need assistance, please reach out to the organizers. If you are concerned about your ability to stand or walk outside during hot temperatures, please stay home!
About Indivisible Greater Vancouver (IGV)
Indivisible Greater Vancouver (IGV) is committed to promoting nonviolent advocacy and activism to create lasting social and political change. Founded in 2017 as a chapter of the national Indivisible movement to resist the Trump agenda, IGV has since expanded its focus to include local and Washington state grassroots organizing.
We work in partnership with organizations that share our values, including Clark County 50501, MoveOn Clark County, LULAC, Pasitos Gigantes, and the Vancouver chapter of the NAACP. Together, we build community power rooted in justice, equity, and solidarity.
IGV is deeply committed to nonviolence as both a principle and a strategy. We at IGV strongly believe that peaceful, nonviolent activism offers social movements the most power to effect change. Through peaceful protests, we set an example of making our voices heard with dignity, empowered by truth. IGV does not condone intimidation, threats, vandalism, interference with access to business or any other lawless actions. If instigators or opponents attempt to violate our commitment to non-violence, we will try to de-escalate and end the event if needed to maintain a safe environment.

You can read more about Indivisible’s national commitment to nonviolence here:
🔗 indivisible.org/commitment-nonviolence
We also value and are guided by the research of Dr. Erica Chenoweth, whose work shows that nonviolent movements are significantly more successful than violent ones in achieving lasting social and political transformation:
🔗 Paths to Resistance – Harvard Kennedy School
Together, we stand strong, peaceful, and resolute—because nonviolence is not passive. It is powerful.

title: Hands Off Social Security
description:
This is a peaceful roadside protest rally hosted by Indivisible McHenry County. It will take place on Thursday, August 14th, from 5:00 p.m. until 7:00 p.m. on the sidewalk on the north side of Route 14 at Teckler Blvd in Crystal Lake, IL. The date was chosen because it's Social Security's 90th anniversary. Please bring your own protest sign or flag. Parking is available in several empty parking lots that are located on the north side of Route 14. Please do not park in front of operating businesses, let's leave those parking spaces open for their customers.

Trump and his administration have repeatedly promised that they are not going to make any changes to Social Security, but that's just another one of their lies. In addition to staff layoffs and other changes which have made it more difficult to access the Social Security office and to apply for benefits, US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent recently let it slip that there are plans to try and privatize Social Security. Millions of us have paid into the system over a lifetime of work and we rely on it for our retirement. Our current government-run Social Security system is inflation proof. Privatizing it would expose us to risky fluctuations in the stock market that could potentially lead to lower or more volatile retirement benefits. If you don't want Social Security to be privatized, please come to this protest rally to voice your objections to privatization and other harmful changes to our Social Security system.

title: Emergency! Save Our Health Care
description:
Emergency! Save Our Health Care is a focused visibility demonstration in support of our local healthcare workers and in opposition to proposed cuts to MediCal that threaten both providers and patients. Participants will fan out along the south side of  E Perkins St at evening rush hour to remind decision‑makers that accessible, quality healthcare is a human right, and to show that we stand shoulder‑to‑shoulder with those who deliver it.

On July 4th, President Trump signed the budget reconciliation package known as the “One Big Beautiful Bill,” which includes approximately $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts over the next decade, and is expected to strip coverage from millions of Americans. Over 40% of Mendocino County residents rely on Medicaid – known in California as MediCal. Cuts to these services would directly impact our community’s ability to access essential medical care. 

“We face a terrible cascade of events,” explains Indivisible Ukiah spokesperson Janet Rosen. “Without MediCal reimbursement, our providers can’t pay their bills. We risk losing our clinics and hospital. If this happens, everything from emergency care to labor and delivery will just disappear.”

Indivisible Ukiah brings neighbors together to defend civil rights, due process, and participatory democracy through peaceful demonstrations and direct action. A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to  nonviolence. We remind all participants to ignore provocations.

title: Bethel Defends Democracy: Homelessness
description:
Please join us for our 23rd consecutive community rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday August 9th, 11am -12:30pm, our focus will be Homelessness. 

“Homeless people are not the problem.  They are the result of the problem.” - unknown

Homelessness is one of America’s most visible yet least understood challenges. It affects people from all walks of life who struggle due to economic hardship, lack of affordable housing, or other systemic barriers. The reality is that most people are forced into homelessness by circumstances beyond their control. The solutions lie in systemic changes, not quick fixes.

Contrary to common narratives, homelessness is not primarily caused by personal factors like addiction or mental illness. These may be precipitating factors for some people, but the homelessness crisis is primarily driven by broader economic and systemic issues, such as: 
Income and public benefits not keeping up with rising housing costs.
Inadequate access to quality healthcare and supportive services.
Systemic racism and marginalization.
 
Our keynote speaker is Rabbi Ari Rosenberg.  He grew up in Waterford, Connecticut and has lived in CT, CA, OH, MA, NJ, and Israel.  He received a BA in English from Rutgers University and he was ordained by Hebrew Union College in 2008.  He served Temple Sholom in New Milford from 2015 to 2020 and is now Executive Director of the Association of Religious Communities ("ARC"), promoting interfaith cooperation to prevent poverty, homelessness and domestic violence throughout the greater Danbury area.  Among other things, ARC is running the only homeless shelter serving the greater Danbury area and placing over 50 clients a year into affordable housing units.  Rabbi Ari also serves as Vice President of New Milford Refugee Resettlement.  He is happily married to Aryn Storrs Rosenberg, and they enjoy their blended family of six in New Milford, CT.

We are very fortunate to welcome our second speaker, Gionnani Gonzalez, a former client of Ari Rosenberg, who will share his personal story.

We are excited to have Pat Lavery as our musician this week.  His band plays their own original music, along with songs that you know but aren’t necessarily the same old bar band repertoire.  He tries to play music that’s fun to dance while being interesting to listen to as well, played with imagination and soul.

The rally is non-partisan. What this means is that like-minded people from diverse backgrounds are participating and are vital to our rallies. Defending Democracy crosses party lines: we have registered Republicans, Unaffiliated, Democrats, and non-voters, all coming together to fight for the rights of “We the People” to determine the type of society we want to live in.

Never miss information about upcoming rallies by registering for our rally newsletter, bit.ly/BethelRalliesNewsletter (case sensitive).  You can also provide feedback on what you'd like to see at future rallies.  Questions and feedback are also always welcome anytime at:
BethelDefendsDemocracyRallies@gmail.com.

We have created a Bethel Rally website that houses all our videos and pictures from the rallies. 

BethelRallies.org

A sign-making table and an information table will also be available.

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

There are 2 small benches at the square and we will have a limited number of camping chairs. Please bring your own lawn or camping chair if you'd like.

Approximate Rally Schedule:

11:00 - 11:15  Assemble and rally at curb (You are welcome to arrive prior to 11:00 for extra curb time)

11:15 - 11:45 Program

11:45 - Noon Rally at curb with chant leader

Noon - 12:20 March with chant leader

12:20   Closing Song

12:30   Disperse

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week. The food pantry greatly appreciates the donations! Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but an updated list of current needs are:

Gravy, condensed soup, any jam or jelly flavor other than grape, baking mixes, and jello. Jello can either be the box mix or predone cups.

Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

SMALL empty detergent bottles

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally. We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking. It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting, marching, themes with speakers, live music, fun trinkets, sign making. We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots. The lot that is very close to the rally location, PT Barnum Square, is behind the municipal center.

Although all street parking is public, we ask that you please not park in the limited parking spots in front of our local businesses, but definitely enjoy our beautiful towns restaurants and shops after the rally! 

Bring your voice, your spirit, and your friends. Let’s make change visible.

💥 Because democracy doesn’t take the summer off.

Thank you 😊

title: Freedom Fridays: STOP THE EPSTEIN COVER-UP
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

ENOUGH IS ENOUGH - RELEASE THE EPSTEIN FILES - THE TRUTH WILL OUT!!! 
Join us on Friday, August 8th at NOON at the Williamsburg James City County Courthouse, located at 5201 Monticello Avenue with your signs, a cold beverage, and a chair if needed.

COMMUNITY NORMS
Please read before attending one of our events.
One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS.
Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. Please remain out of the median, per instructions from the police. Being in the median puts us at risk and potentially drivers as well. 
If an Urgent Situation arises, we will raise a straight arm with our Hand in a Fist to ask for Silence. PLEASE DO THE SAME TO QUIET THE CROWD. This way we can quickly relay an important message to all. 
We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day.” 	
At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept.
Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS!
If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!
As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers, who will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts and an Indivisible Cap or Tricorn Hat. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. 
Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk.
We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

title: Visibility Brigade - North Park

location.venue: Meade Ave bridge over I-805 in North Park

description:
Meet on the Meade Ave bridge over I-805. 

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving. 

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

www.VisibilityBrigade.com

See you at 5:00!

title: SOS! Save Our Seats Protest at Indiana Governor's Mansion
description:
Indivisible Central Indiana is announcing an emergency rally —“SOS: Save Our Seats”— to coincide with Vice President J.D. Vance’s visit to the Hoosier state on Thursday, August 7, 2025, from 4 - 6 pm at the Governor’s mansion. Vance’s closed-door meeting with Governor Mike Braun is likely aimed at securing a special legislative session to redraw Indiana’s congressional map and eliminate the state’s two Democratic seats. Indiana already tilts 7-to-2 for the GOP in Congress, and outside operatives want to eliminate the voice of the people. 

Mid-cycle redistricting is usually reserved for the history books, yet GOP strategists are reviving it from Texas to Indiana to lock in power before 2026 because they know their dangerous actions are so unpopular with a majority of Americans. As the Wall Street Journal noted, “Former President Donald Trump has catalyzed a nationwide scramble … by pushing a mid-decade redistricting effort in Texas, aiming to add five new Republican congressional seats.” The Brennan Center warns that existing gerrymanders already “give Republicans an advantage of around 16 House seats” even under today’s maps—an edge that could grow if more states follow Texas’s lead. 

Vice-President J.D. Vance’s trip to Indianapolis is part of that playbook; Governor Mike Braun conceded that national operatives are “going to come into every state that’s got the possibility of that happening,” with Indiana’s lone competitive district in the crosshairs. Voting-rights advocates say the push echoes the 2003 Texas power grab later struck down in court and amounts to an “extraordinary power grab” that would silence diverse communities, erode public trust, and reshape Congress for the rest of the decade.

Indivisible Central Indiana encourages Hoosiers to join us outside of the Governor’s Mansion to peacefully protest this clear power grab to take away voters’ voices. 

When: Thursday, August 7, 2025
Time: 4-6 p.m. ET
Location: Governor’s Mansion, 4750 N Meridian St, Indianapolis, IN 46208

title: I91 Overpass Visibility Standout - Longmeadow

location.venue: Bark Haul Road (at the I91 overpass)

description:
How to Get There The address Bark Haul Road will get you there if you're using Waze. (Bark Haul Road is off Route 5.) The event is on the I-91 overpass. There's plenty of parking, although you can't park on the overpass.

If You Bring a Sign, Banner, or Flag For sign and banner lettering, bigger is better, so it can be easily read from the roadway. Flags are great, too. Wouldn't it be amazing to reclaim our flag? Mass DOT does not like things attached to the fence. They may visit, so be prepared to not have anything attached. Never drape anything over the fence, even with ropes, because it would be very dangerous if it accidentally fell onto the highway. Other Logistics No Port-A-Potties are available. Please take everything you brought away with you and leave the site totally clean. About These Standouts

Come join like-minded folks to demand that Trump, Musk, and the Republican-led Congress stop their unconstitutional power grab and the cruel destruction of our federal government.

We will hold banners, signs, and flags, and we'll wave to passing motorists. Many will beep and wave back at us, which feels nice! We'll show people that they're not alone and help give them the courage to join us and take a stand.

Please come out whether or not you have a sign or banner or flag. More people is better!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 hour and 15 minute standout.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational and non-violent, in words and body language. 

We welcome your energy and ideas, and we're looking forward to meeting everyone. Let's have some fun and make some good trouble

title: Four Corners in Lenexa  Standing Rally
description: As citizens, we can’t let the policies and actions of the Federal Government and unelected billionaires be normalized, but we can only stop what’s going on by coming together.  A STANDING RALLY  will draw attention to the situation, encouraging our neighbors to join with us. We will rally every Saturday morning from 11 AM – 12 PM.  Stay for the full hour or come by when and for how long you can. We will peacefully line the sidewalk on all four corners of 87th Parkway and Maurer Road,  holding signs on issues that are most meaningful to us or just simply standing in support of our neighbors and our country.  If sitting is more comfortable for you, you are very welcome to bring mobility or lawn chairs!! There is room for everyone!
accessibility_notes:
Here are a couple of notes on logistics.
Please be especially mindful of parking.  For example, if you live relatively nearby, please consider walking.  If you drive, there is street parking on the residential streets to the north and also a bit further on the south.  About ½ mile down on the west, there is a large civic campus garage at 17201 W 87th St. Pkwy.  In addition, on the SE, SW, and NW sides of the intersection, there are restaurants and shops with big, but commercially owned parking lots meant for customers. Note that Lenexa Point on the NW side has recently put up signs, saying they will tow non-customer cars. (Also note that if you become a customer, it’s fine to bring snacks to the rally that you have bought, but please take any empty snack containers back home with you, when you leave. In any case, no matter which direction you are coming from, if it is possible, please try to park before you reach the intersection to save on congestion and choose a spot as far away as you feel comfortable walking from, leaving closer spots to those who can’t walk as far.
The rally will start on the SE corner, but as more folks arrive, we will disperse to the SW, NW, and NE corners, as well.   If you cross from one side to another, please pay particular attention to cars turning right as you cross! 
 Participants should bring their own signs (if they want to hold them).  Note that sticks supporting the signs can’t be pointed at either end.  Also, in designing content for the signs, please remember that children will be present.  
Please stand only along the sidewalks parallel to the street and not on the grass.  However, also be sure to allow pedestrian access to the sidewalk and businesses.   We are not expecting issues, but keep in mind that a core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action.  Remember to de-escalate any potential confrontation with someone,  who disagrees with you. And of course, follow directions from our excellent Lenexa police, if asked.
We will not have speakers. The plan will simply be to hold the signs we have made and wave, if that feels right.  We expect that a lot of passing cars will honk back in approval! 
Finally, please note that all our organizers will be wearing lanyards with badges reading  “Standing Rally Corner Captain or “Standing Rally Media/City Liaison”.  If you see other folks with “Press” marked on their clothing or who are giving direction to you, know that they are not part of Four Corners and are not endorsed or vetted by us.
See you soon.  Let’s show our neighbors “what Democracy Looks Like”!!
P.S.  If you want to post an inspiring (!) story about your experience, please add #FourCornersinLenexa to your post!

We gather weekly and show a message to passing cars on high visibility areas like freeway overpasses. You can bring your own signs but they're not required. We raise some larger Indivisible banners and spell out a short message in 2 foot tall letters. Then, we stand and wave at passing cars and chat about the movement and anything else. We stay about 2 hours, covering some high traffic time like rush hour. It's an easy and fun way to spread your message and meet fellow activists.

This week's will be at the Market Street overpass of I-205. You can park on Market street nearby and walk at most 2 blocks up a gentle hill. The street address I gave for this event is a good area to park.

title: Protest Elon Musk's Illegal Government Takeover #TeslaTakedown - Stanford Saturdays
description:
PLEASE READ COMPLETELY before attending!

This is a peaceful, nonviolent protest on the sidewalk in front of the Stanford Tesla showroom. There will be theatrics and dancing. Get ready to improv! We'll also be looping through Stanford Shopping Mall with peaceful positive energy. Of course you may opt out and continue to demonstrate in front of the Tesla showroom. 

We know making lots of noise is typically part of a good protest. But most protests aren’t right across the street from a Ronald McDonald House. Let’s take care to keep our noise levels down to a dull roar. Bring your energy and spirit, but let’s refrain from the cowbells, drums and car honks. We can get our point across without interfering with our neighbors on the other side of the road.

Wear your favorite wig, big hat, or costume. We want to have fun and to feel like a party during our demonstrations! Signs, flags, and similar items are welcome.

This is a peaceful demonstration, and any conflicts or altercations will not be tolerated. Walk away if one arises and report it to the demonstration leader on site if it is a serious altercation. We will comply with requests from the police and mall security, including if we are asked to leave. By the way, we have already have a fantastic relationship with mall security, which is a plus!

Do not boo or confront Tesla drivers or cars, or Tesla employees. Remember that most Tesla drivers are our allies, and many are protesting with us!

Please Note: Photos may be taken and published at this event, including by attendees and professional photographers. If you prefer not to have your image captured or shared, please take your own precautions (e.g., wear a mask, hat, or wig).

#BoycottTesla #DivestFromTesla

title: Defend the Constitution, Stop Avelo, Abolish ICE! Lakeland, FL

address_lines: Harden Blvd & Town Center Dr, Near Starbucks

description:
# 🦅 Defend the Constitution 🛑 Stop Avelo ⛓️‍💥 Abolish ICE 🧊 Save the Everglades 🐊
*Hosted by DEFUND OLIGARCHY · BLESSED BY LIBERTY · INDIVISIBLE*
([en español](https://mobilize.us/s/skrhfa))

#### Non-Partisan Public Demonstration — Saturday, Jul 26, 2025
##### Lakeland, FL

# 📢 THIS IS NOT YOUR TYPICAL FREEDOM OF SPEECH EVENT
##### Read all instructions

We are taking a stand against Avelo Airlines’ $150 million contract with ICE to operate deportation flights. These flights are facilitating the removal of individuals without due process — violating the core principles of our republic.

This is a call to action. We’re joining forces to demand that Avelo cancel its ICE contract and end its involvement in unconstitutional deportations.

# 🪧 Our Demands
✈️ Avelo Airlines: End your contract with ICE — now.

✊ It’s ICE or us.

You cannot serve both the people and an agency that tears families apart, starves humans, withholds water, denies medical care, kills people, forces humans into slavery, performs sterilizations without consent, and refuses to recognize U.S. birth certificates and REAL ID.

If you choose ICE, we will end your public subsidies and taxpayer-funded support.

✊ Polk County residents: Boycott Avelo & anyone profiting from ICE

✊ City of Lakeland: Stop giving Avelo $30,000 a year in marketing handouts.

✊ Polk County: Cancel the $6 million corporate welfare deal with Avelo.

✊ DHS & James Uthmeier: No Alligator Alley Concentration Camp. No cages on sacred ground. 🐊

✊ ICE: Stay out of Florida. Stop terrorizing schools, hospitals, courthouses, and workplaces. End detention. Deport only violent offenders with criminal convictions.

✊ LPD & PCSO: Do not cooperate with ICE. Arrest ICE agents operating without signed judicial warrants for violent criminal offenders.

✊ Sheriff Grady Judd: Release a public statement denouncing ICE and pledge to support Polk County residents who stand their ground against ICE.

✊Scott Franklin, Rick Scott, Ashley Moody: Defund & abolish ICE. 

✊ Florida State Legislature: Ban the use of taxpayer money for ICE operations. Pass legislation banning cooperation with ICE beyond what federal law requires.


# 🛑 WHY WE’RE PROTESTING

❌ Avelo is enabling illegal detentions and deportations without hearings.

❌U.S. citizens and work permit holders — like Juan Carlos Lopez-Gomez and Heidy Sanchez Tejeda — have been detained without cause.

❌DHS & ICE have unilaterally seized protected land in the Everglades to create a 5,000-person prison with no A/C and no access to lawyers by raiding FEMA and charging the state $450 million, despite the objections of county and tribal leadership. 

❌Children are being separated from parents, denied legal representation, and even deported during active custody disputes — like two-year-old citizen known as V.M.L.

❌Our Constitutional rights — due process, legal counsel, protection from executive overreach — are being ignored.

# ✨ WE STAND FOR:
- Families
- Immigration rights
- Due process
- Constitutional liberty for all
- Holding corporations accountable for profiting from human suffering

# 🗓️ EVENT DETAILS

📍 Lakeland, FL (exact meetup location will be emailed after RSVP)

🕒 Saturday, Aug 30, 2025, 6 pm - 8 pm

🎨 Signs provided (but feel free to bring your own especially if it highlights the case of individuals who have been unlawfully detained or removed)

👍Be alert: impersonators and fake news outlets posing as independent media may be present. Verify credentials before giving an interview.

👍Don’t engage with trolls or agitators. They may pretend to be a fellow protester.

👍Focus your energy on building unity and protecting our democratic, constitutional republic.

title: ¡Alto a Avelo, Acabemos con ICE! Lakeland, FL

description:
# 🦅 Defendamos la Constitución 🛑 Alto a Avelo ⛓️‍💥 Acabemos con ICE 🧊
*Organizado por DESFINANCIAR A LA OLIGARQUÍA · BENDICIÓN DE LA LIBERTAD · INDIVISIBLES*
[in English](https://mobilize.us/s/3PHiaS)

### Demostración Pública No Partidista — Sábado, 30 de agosto de 2025
#### Lakeland, Florida

# 📢 ESTO NO ES TU TÍPICO EVENTO DE LIBERTAD DE EXPRESIÓN
#### Asegúrate de leer todas las instrucciones

Nos estamos levantando contra el contrato de 150 millones de dólares entre Avelo Airlines y ICE (la agencia de migración de EE.UU.) para operar vuelos de deportación. Estos vuelos están facilitando la expulsión de personas sin el debido proceso legal — lo que va en contra de los principios fundamentales de la república.

Este es un llamado urgente a la acción. Nos estamos organizando para exigir que Avelo cancele su contrato con ICE y deje de participar en deportaciones inconstitucionales.

# 🪧 Nuestras demandas
✈️ Avelo Airlines: Terminen su contrato con ICE — ahora.

Es ICE o nosotros.

No se puede servir al pueblo y al mismo tiempo a una agencia que separa familias, priva de alimentos a personas, niega acceso al agua, atención médica, causa muertes, impone condiciones de esclavitud, realiza esterilizaciones sin consentimiento y se niega a reconocer certificados de nacimiento estadounidenses ni identificaciones oficiales.

Si eligen a ICE, cancelaremos sus subsidios públicos y el apoyo financiado por los contribuyentes.

✊ Residentes del Condado de Polk: Boicoteen a ICE y a cualquier empresa que se beneficie de sus actividades.

✊ Ciudad de Lakeland: Dejen de otorgar a Avelo $30,000 anuales en incentivos de mercadeo.

✊ Condado de Polk: Cancelen el acuerdo de $6 millones en beneficios corporativos con Avelo.

✊ DHS y James Uthmeier: No a la “Alcatraz de los caimanes”. No a las jaulas en tierras sagradas.

✊ ICE: Fuera de Florida. Dejen de aterrorizar escuelas, hospitales, tribunales y lugares de trabajo. Pongan fin a la detención. Deporten solo a delincuentes violentos con condenas penales.

✊ LPD y PCSO: No cooperen con ICE. Arresten a los agentes de ICE que operen sin órdenes judiciales firmadas para casos de delitos violentos.

✊ Sheriff Grady Judd: Emita una declaración pública denunciando a ICE y comprométase a apoyar a los residentes del Condado de Polk que se enfrenten a ICE.

✊ Scott Franklin, Rick Scott, Ashley Moody: Recorten los fondos y abolan ICE.

✊ Legislatura del Estado de Florida: Prohíban el uso de dinero de los contribuyentes para operaciones de ICE. Aprueben leyes que prohíban la cooperación con ICE más allá de lo que exige la ley federal.

# 🛑 ¿POR QUÉ PROTESTAMOS?

❌ Avelo está colaborando con detenciones ilegales y deportaciones sin audiencia legal.

❌ Ciudadanos estadounidenses y personas con permisos de trabajo — como Juan Carlos López-Gómez y Heidy Sánchez Tejeda — han sido detenidos sin justificación.

❌ Hay niños que están siendo separados de sus padres, sin acceso a abogados, e incluso deportados mientras todavía están en medio de procesos legales por custodia — como el caso de una niña ciudadana estadounidense de dos años conocida como V.M.L.

❌ Se están violando nuestros derechos constitucionales: el debido proceso, el derecho a defensa legal, y la protección frente a abusos del poder ejecutivo.

# ✨ NOSOTROS DEFENDEMOS:

- A las familias
- Los derechos de las personas migrantes
- El debido proceso
- Las libertades constitucionales para todxs
- La responsabilidad de las empresas que lucran con el sufrimiento humano

👍 Nuestro compromiso es con la no violencia. Este será un acto pacífico. Sé respetuoso en todo momento.

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:
General Visibility Rules:
•	Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
•	"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
•	Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:
•	Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
•	Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
•	High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
o	Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
o	Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
o	Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
•	Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
•	Material and Construction:
o	Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
o	Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
o	Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
•	Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
•	Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Weekly (Fri) Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
description:
Wow! What a great location for a standout! On 5/30, around 17 people, including a bagpiper!  What a blast! LOTS of engagement with motorists!

There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all! 

We'll have letterboards prepared for the lower part of the overpass fencing - the photo shows how that will look to folks passing on the Mass Pike. We're interacting with motorists on the Mass Pike, and on Southampton Road. We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 1/2 hours.

### How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass. 

### Parking

We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and it seems that parking would be OK there.

It looks like The Wealth Technology Group has vacated their office at 130 Southampton Rd, but the internet says that other businesses are located there, so please be mindful if you decide to park there.

### Etiquette!

We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too. 

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!
